.claude/reference/ui/components/ribbon/RibbonScope.md:14:A tab whose commands work on one of the chat input's modes, as the Code and Spec tabs do, takes that mode's colour: its label is in the mode's colour while the tab is closed, and while open, the tab is tinted with it instead and its label is the tab's own colour. Each such tab says more. Its tabs are, in order: Project, Code, Spec, Research, and Application. The window always opens on Project. Beneath the tabs, the selected tab's commands sit in groups. There is no raw output view and no toggle for one.
.claude/reference/ui/components/ribbon/RibbonScope.md:18:<Alt+1> opens the first tab, <Alt+2> the second, and so on, through each tab in the order the tabs are shown, <Alt+5> opening Application. Each opens its tab alone, as clicking it does, and expands the ribbon first if it is collapsed. A number past the last tab does nothing. Like the ribbon's other shortcuts, they do nothing while an inset panel is open. A tab's tooltip doesn't give its shortcut, since a tab has no tooltip.
.claude/reference/ui/components/ribbon/RibbonScope.md:24:Double-clicking a tab still collapses the ribbon, and expanding it again shows the same tabs open. Which tabs are open isn't kept between launches: the window always opens with only Project open.
.claude/reference/ui/components/ribbon/RibbonScope.md:28:At the left end of the bar, left of the tab bar itself rather than inside it, so the tab bar's own padding and bottom line don't reach it, sits the left container. It holds, in order, the project indicator, the collapse chevron, and the activity spinner, and can hold other things after them. It is the same whether the ribbon is expanded, beside the tabs, or collapsed, leading the row of primary commands.
.claude/reference/ui/components/ribbon/RibbonScope.md:33:At the right end of the bar, right of the tabs, or of the primary commands when the ribbon is collapsed, sits the right container. It holds nothing yet, and can hold other things. It lays out what it holds as the left container does: vertically centred, with no gap between things and no padding around them, shrinking to fit, and not there at all while it holds nothing, as it is now.
.claude/reference/ui/components/ribbon/RibbonScope.md:37:The indicator and list of the [RunningActivityScope](../../../scope/running-activity/RunningActivityScope.md) sit in the left container, just right of the collapse chevron. While nothing is running, the spinner isn't there, and the left container shrinks around the project indicator and the chevron.
.claude/reference/ui/components/ribbon/RibbonScope.md:41:The [ProjectIndicator](../project-indicator/ProjectIndicator.md) leads the left container, a solid block the full height of the bar. There is no divider between it and what follows: the change of background is the edge. The collapse chevron sits just after it, and the activity spinner just after the chevron.
.claude/reference/ui/components/ribbon/RibbonScope.md:78:- small: only in the collapsed ribbon: 22 pixels tall, its small icon to the left of its label, and only as wide as they are
.claude/reference/ui/components/ribbon/RibbonScope.md:95:The ribbon collapses, and expands again, with a chevron button in the left container, after the project indicator, by double-clicking a tab, or with Ctrl+F1 (Cmd+F1 on macOS). Whether it is collapsed is one of the [UserPreferencesScope](../../../scope/user-preferences/UserPreferencesScope.md).
.claude/reference/ui/components/ribbon/RibbonScope.md:96:Collapsed, the tabs go away too. The ribbon becomes a single thin row led by the left container, the same as beside the tabs, the project indicator filling the row's height, and then every primary command, from all of the tabs, as small buttons: a small icon beside its label, and dark mode as a small switch in a block only as wide as the switch and its label. Every one is only as wide as its own icon and label, 8 pixels from the next, whatever the tab it comes from calls it; a command that is slim in its tab doesn't grow to fill the row. They keep the order of their tabs, with a thin vertical divider between the commands of one tab and the next, and keep their tooltips and disabled states. The right container, when it holds anything, ends the row. Every control in the row, the dividers and the containers' contents included, is vertically centred in it.
.claude/reference/ui/components/ribbon/RibbonScope.md:97:When the commands and dividers are wider than the room between the left container and the right container, or the right end of the row, that stretch of the row scrolls sideways, as the expanded command area does. The containers stay where they are, never scrolled away or squeezed, and nothing in the row shrinks to fit.

content.content:
launches: the window always opens with only Project open.

    leftContainer:
        At the left end of the bar, left of the tab bar itself rather than
        inside it, so the tab bar's own padding and bottom line don't reach
        it, sits the left container. It holds, in order, the project
        indicator, the collapse chevron, and the activity spinner, and can
        hold other things after them. It is the same whether the ribbon is
        expanded, beside the tabs, or collapsed, leading the row of primary
        commands.

        Everything in it is vertically centred in the bar, with no gap
        between one thing and the next and no padding around them: each
        thing's own size is all the room it takes. The container shrinks to
        fit what it holds, and when it holds nothing, it isn't there at all.

    rightContainer:
        At the right end of the bar, right of the tabs, or of the primary
        commands when the ribbon is collapsed, sits the right container. It
        holds nothing yet, and can hold other things. It lays out what it
        holds as the left container does: vertically centred, with no gap
        between things and no padding around them, shrinking to fit, and not
        there at all while it holds nothing, as it is now.

    activity:
        The indicator and list of the @{RunningActivityScope} sit in the left
        container, just right of the collapse chevron. While nothing is
        running, the spinner isn't there, and the left container shrinks
        around the project indicator and the chevron.

    projectIndicator:
        The @{ProjectIndicator} leads the left container, a solid block the
        full height of the bar. There is no divider between it and what
        follows: the change of background is the edge. The collapse chevron
        sits just after it, and the activity spinner just after the
        chevron.

    groups:
        Each group has its title in muted text rotated -90deg (bottom to top)
        with each title centred down its strip whatever that height is.

    collapsing:
        The ribbon collapses, and expands again, with a chevron button in the
        left container, after the project indicator, by double-clicking a tab, or with Ctrl+F1
        (Cmd+F1 on macOS). Whether it is collapsed is one of the
        @{UserPreferencesScope}.

- [Left container items are vertically centred with no gap or padding; each takes only its own size](spec/ui/components/ribbon/index.pi)
- [The collapse chevron is a square button, 22 pixels on each side](spec/ui/components/ribbon/index.pi)
- [The chevron is the same size, and its icon the same size, expanded and collapsed](spec/ui/components/ribbon/index.pi)
- [The collapsed row's small commands are 22 pixels tall](.claude/reference/ui/components/ribbon/RibbonScope.md)
- [Every control in the collapsed row, the chevron included, is vertically centred in it](.claude/reference/ui/components/ribbon/RibbonScope.md)
- [Collapsing and expanding use the chevron, a tab double-click, or Ctrl+F1](.claude/reference/ui/components/ribbon/RibbonScope.md)

use /lib
from /ui/theme import ThemeScope
use /ui
from /ui/components/project-indicator import ProjectIndicator
from ./project-tab import RibbonProjectTabScope
from ./code-tab import RibbonCodeTabScope
from ./spec-tab import RibbonSpecTabScope
from ./research-tab import RibbonResearchTabScope
from ./application-tab import RibbonApplicationTabScope
from /scope/running-activity import RunningActivityScope
from /scope/user-preferences import UserPreferencesScope

export ui-component RibbonScope:
    concept: {RibbonConcept}

concept RibbonConcept:
    pitch:
        The ribbon along the top of the main window: tabs, each holding the
        application's commands for one area of work in labelled groups.

    shape: {RibbonShape}

shape RibbonShape:
    description:
        A ribbon runs along the top of the window, using gpui-kit's Tab
        component with its default styling, borders, and spacing, only in the
        @{ThemeScope}'s colours. Nothing adds to or takes away from a tab's own
        borders or margins, so a tab's label never shifts as tabs open and
        close. Along the top of the commands, a line in the colour of the tabs'
        own side borders runs from the far left, beneath the project indicator
        and the rest of the left container, to the side border of the first open tab, and on from that tab's other
        side border to the next open tab or the far right. An open tab meets
        the commands beneath it with no line between them, its side borders
        running straight down to where the line picks up again. There is no
        other line there, not even a faint one at a fractional display scale.

        A tab whose commands work on one of the chat input's modes, as the Code
        and Spec tabs do, takes that mode's colour: its label is in the mode's
        colour while the tab is closed, and while open, the tab is tinted with
        it instead and its label is the tab's own colour. Each such tab says
        more. Its tabs are, in order: Project,
        Code, Spec, Research, and Application. The window always opens on
        Project. Beneath the tabs, the selected tab's commands sit in groups.
        There is no raw output view and no toggle for one.

    keyboard:
        <Alt+1> opens the first tab, <Alt+2> the second, and so on, through
        each tab in the order the tabs are shown, <Alt+5> opening Application.
        Each opens its tab alone, as clicking it does, and expands the ribbon
        first if it is collapsed. A number past the last tab does nothing. Like
        the ribbon's other shortcuts, they do nothing while an inset panel is
        open. A tab's tooltip doesn't give its shortcut, since a tab has no
        tooltip.

    openingSeveralTabs:
        Clicking a tab opens it alone, as usual. Ctrl+clicking one (Cmd+click on
        macOS) opens it alongside whichever tabs are already open, or, if it is
        already open, closes it, so any number of tabs can be open at once. The
        last open tab can't be closed this way: Ctrl+clicking it leaves it open.
        Every open tab shows as selected.

        The command area then holds the groups of every open tab side by side,
        in the order of the tabs rather than the order they were opened, with no
        divider between one tab's groups and the next, as between any groups. An
        open tab with no commands adds nothing, and "No commands yet" shows only
        when none of the open tabs has any. When the groups are wider than the
        window, the command area scrolls sideways. The command area stays the
        same height however many tabs are open.

        Double-clicking a tab still collapses the ribbon, and expanding it again
        shows the same tabs open. Which tabs are open isn't kept between
        launches: the window always opens with only Project open.

    leftContainer:
        At the left end of the bar, left of the tab bar itself rather than
        inside it, so the tab bar's own padding and bottom line don't reach
        it, sits the left container. It holds, in order, the project
        indicator, the collapse chevron, and the activity spinner, and can
        hold other things after them. It is the same whether the ribbon is
        expanded, beside the tabs, or collapsed, leading the row of primary
        commands.

        Everything in it is vertically centred in the bar, with no gap
        between one thing and the next and no padding around them: each
        thing's own size is all the room it takes. The container shrinks to
        fit what it holds, and when it holds nothing, it isn't there at all.

    rightContainer:
        At the right end of the bar, right of the tabs, or of the primary
        commands when the ribbon is collapsed, sits the right container. It
        holds nothing yet, and can hold other things. It lays out what it
        holds as the left container does: vertically centred, with no gap
        between things and no padding around them, shrinking to fit, and not
        there at all while it holds nothing, as it is now.

    activity:
        The indicator and list of the @{RunningActivityScope} sit in the left
        container, just right of the collapse chevron. While nothing is
        running, the spinner isn't there, and the left container shrinks
        around the project indicator and the chevron.

    projectIndicator:
        The @{ProjectIndicator} leads the left container, a solid block the
        full height of the bar. There is no divider between it and what
        follows: the change of background is the edge. The collapse chevron
        sits just after it, and the activity spinner just after the
        chevron.

    groups:
        Each group has its title in muted text rotated -90deg (bottom to top)
        aligned along the left edge of the group naming what its commands have
        in common. The title sits on a strip with a slightly different
        background colour, at 12px, with generous padding either side of it
        within the strip, which runs the full height of the commands' area, with
        no padding above or below it, 8 pixels from the buttons beside it. The
        first group's strip sits flush against the left edge of the commands'
        area, with no space before it. Groups sit side by side, 8 pixels apart, with no
        divider between them: each group's title strip is what marks where it
        starts.

        A tab with no commands reads "No commands yet".

    tabs:
        Each tab is a scope of its own, which says what groups and commands it
        holds, and what each command does.

        project: @{RibbonProjectTabScope}

        code: @{RibbonCodeTabScope}

        spec: @{RibbonSpecTabScope}

        research: @{RibbonResearchTabScope}

        application: @{RibbonApplicationTabScope}

    commands:
        A command button is one of two sizes, and each tab says which of its
        commands are which:
        - full: its large icon above its label, exactly two slim buttons stacked tall
        - slim: 22 pixels tall, its small icon to the left of its label
        - small: only in the collapsed ribbon: 22 pixels tall, its small icon to the left of its label, and only as wide as they are

        Buttons side by side are 8 pixels apart. Slim buttons side by side
        stack down instead, top aligned, two to a column, each column as wide
        as its widest button and each button as wide as its column; a third
        starts the next column, 8 pixels along. A full button always stands
        alone. A slim button fills only its column's width: nowhere does a
        button stretch to fill a row.

        Every command starts from the top of its group, so the commands of a
        tab all start at the same line. A full button is always two slim
        buttons stacked tall, never shorter or taller, however much its icon
        and label would take, alone or beside any column.

        Every button is square, with no rounded corners. Its background is
        clearly apart from the commands' area behind it, though still quiet:
        white laid a seventh of the way over that area in dark mode, and not
        quite half way in light mode, rather than a colour of its own, so it
        stays as far apart from a tinted body too, lighter in both modes, and more so while hovered; while
        pressed it darkens instead. An on or off setting, like dark mode, is a
        switch rather than a button, sitting in a block with a button's
        colour, as wide as a button of its size and as tall as the switch and
        its label need.

        A command's tooltip explains what it does rather than repeating its
        label, and gives its keyboard shortcut if it has one.

        A command can be marked primary; each tab says which of its commands
        are.

        A command that can't run is disabled, not hidden, and its tooltip says
        why.

    height:
        The commands drive the height: the command area is as tall as the
        tallest column of the open tabs, padded 8 pixels above and below, and
        nothing more. Since no column holds more than two slim buttons, and a
        full button is two slim buttons tall, the tallest the command area gets
        is two slim buttons with 8 pixels between them, padded: 68 pixels, and
        never more. A tab whose tallest column is two slim buttons, or that has
        a full button, is taller than one of a single slim button, and a tab
        with no commands,
        which is only its "No commands yet" padded the same way, is the
        shortest of all. So switching tabs can change the command area's
        height, and the window beneath moves with it.

        Every group is as tall as the command area, so the groups' title strips
        run its full height whichever tab is open.

        There are 8 pixels of padding at the right end but none at the left:
        the first group's title strip starts right at the command area's left
        edge. "No commands yet" keeps 8 pixels from that edge. The groups'
        title strips are not padded, and run the command area's full height,
        with each title centred down its strip whatever that height is.

    collapsing:
        The ribbon collapses, and expands again, with a chevron button in the
        left container, after the project indicator, by double-clicking a tab, or with Ctrl+F1
        (Cmd+F1 on macOS). Whether it is collapsed is one of the
        @{UserPreferencesScope}.

        Collapsed, the tabs go away too. The ribbon becomes a single thin row
        led by the left container, the same as beside the tabs, the project
        indicator filling the row's height, and then every primary command, from all of
        the tabs, as small buttons: a small icon beside its label, and dark mode
        as a small switch in a block only as wide as the switch and its label.
        Every one is only as wide as its own icon and label, 8 pixels from the
        next, whatever the tab it comes from calls it; a command that is slim
        in its tab doesn't grow to fill the row. They keep the order of their
        tabs, with a thin vertical divider between the commands of one tab and
        the next, and keep their tooltips and disabled states. The right
        container, when it holds anything, ends the row. Every control in the
        row, the dividers and the containers' contents included, is
        vertically centred in it.

        When the commands and dividers are wider than the room between the
        left container and the right container, or the right end of the row,
        that stretch of the row scrolls sideways, as the expanded command area
        does. The containers stay where they are, never scrolled away or
        squeezed, and nothing in the row shrinks to fit.
